newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT- UBS cuts Cascade to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT- UBS cuts Cascade to hold.

text.p: -- UBS Securites analyst Nikos Theodosopoulos cut Cascade Communications Corp to hold from buy, citing concern about slowing growth in Cascade's core switching business and an unexpected rise in accounts receivables in the fourth quarter.

-- In published comments, the analyst said the company's fourth quarter results were back-loaded to an unexpected degree, which may suggest the company had had difficulties producing the results expected of it by Wall Street.
-- He noted that the company's fourth quarter earnings of $0.24 per share were slightly ahead of the Wall Street range of $0.22 to $0.23 per share.
-- He said Cascade's fourth quarter accounts receivable days sales outstanding (DSO) were up 21 days to 68 days compared to the third quarter.

-- Rising DSOs are considered a sign that a company may have granted more generous credit terms to customers so as to book sales earlier. In Cascade's case, this could allow it to sacrifice future earnings in order to boost fourth quarter results.

-- Theodosopoulos said he was maintaining his 1997 earnings estimate of $1.10 per share and 1998 estimate of $1.62 per share, but had adjusted his 1997 estimates to reflect his expectation of a more back-loaded year.
-- The UBS analyst concerns echoed those of other analysts who participated in a conference call Thursday with Cascade following the release of the company's fourth quarter results.
-- "While we believe Cascade has excellent technology and a strong management team, the lack of near-term visibility leads us to a hold rating for now," he wrote.
-- "We would upgrade the stock upon better visibility into the launch of the AX product and the outlook for the 8000/9000 product in 1997," he said.

-- AX is the name for the company's recently introduced line of remote access concentrators, a new business for the company. The 8000/9000 product is the company's core frame-relay switching product used by telecommunciation companies for high-speed data communications.
